captures.description: THE OXYRHYNCHUS PAPYRI, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'a massive collection of ancient manuscripts discovered in the garbage dumps of Oxyrhynchus (modern Bahnasa, Egypt) by Oxford classicists Bernard Grenfell and Arthur Hunt between 1896 and 1907.' The collection (EES, Oxford, 'an estimated 500,000 fragments'), the period, the languages, the content mix (90% documents, 10% literary and religious, 'early Christian gospels, and biblical fragments (such as Papyrus 52 and the Gospel of Thomas)'), the publication series. Seven cards: the collection's own Oxford page, Wikipedia, the EES, four videos.
